name: fs-scope-deny-mirror
body:
The acting agent's `edit`-action rules in its opencode 2.x `permissions` array are evaluated in array order: an allow rule grants the path, a deny rule revokes it, the last matching rule wins, and a path matched by zero rules is refused (deny-by-default). The fs tools' per-path scope (`apg_rm`/`apg_mv`/`apg_cp`) equals this effective scope, resolved together with the candidate in one main-anchored frame, so the fs scope stays within the agent's `edit` scope. A code-writer path that resolves into the main checkout is refused independently.

The fs tools read both allow and deny entries as ordered rules: `opencode-suite/lib/apg.ts` reads the agent's `permissions` array, selects the `edit`-action rules into ordered `{glob, allow}[]` (`editAllowGlobs`, `readAgentEditGlobs`, `agentFsGlobs`), and `fsScopeDecision` decides by the last matching rule (allow permits, deny refuses, zero match refuses). `opencode-suite/tools/apg_rm.ts`, `apg_mv.ts`, and `apg_cp.ts` consume that ordered rule list. `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md` describes the fs tools' scope as the effective allow-plus-deny scope with last match wins, so a sibling cross-denial holds for the fs tools as it holds for `edit`.
